title: The logic of the past hypothesis
version: PhilSci-Archive preprint, deposited 10 Nov 2011 (30 pp.); printed as ch. of The Probability Map of the Universe (Harvard UP 2023), DOI 10.4159/9780674287716-004 (Crossref metadata, printed version not read)
locators: Abstract; Sec. 1 (two Albert theses); Sec. 4 (coarse-graining irreversibility, Gibbs entropy non-decreasing); Sec. 6 (Simple Past Hypothesis, classical); Sec. 7 (quantum version; Past Law Hypothesis)
assumptions: TRI microdynamics; a fixed coarse-graining; Simple Dynamical Conjecture (macro-level predictability); objective probability over initial states
conclusion: Authors' claims: some Past-Hypothesis-type posit is necessary for irreversible macrodynamics; the Hypothesis is an objective probability distribution over the initial state (quantum: initial state is 'Simple'), not a constraint on the early Universe's entropy; under extra assumptions it amounts to a Past Law Hypothesis
proof_status: Author's derivations read at stated locators; no independent reproduction
open_questions: Differences between the 2011 preprint and the printed 2023 chapter; whether 'Simple' can be made precise without circularity (Brown 2017's objection)
relevance: The central recent statement of what the PH must be; directly checks the paper's PH formulation in main.tex sec:direction
limits: Preprint version read, not the printed chapter; exa PDF extraction may drop some formatting; no independent check of the statistical-mechanics claims

title: The Thermodynamic Arrow: Puzzles and Pseudo-puzzles
version: arXiv:physics/0402040v1 (2004-02-06, only version); related printed version in Time and Matter proceedings (2006), DOI 10.1142/9789812774392_0015 (Crossref metadata, not read)
locators: Secs. 1-2 (T-asymmetry puzzle; kaon objection answered via PCT); sec. on one-asymmetry model (Boltzmann response to Loschmidt); 'Which is the right model?'; Gold-universe section ('what right do we have to assume...'); 'Scepticism about the second law'
assumptions: The statistics of SM are time-symmetric; explanatory symmetry (double standard) as methodological constraint
conclusion: Authors' claims: two competing conceptions of the puzzle (one-asymmetry vs two-asymmetry); one-asymmetry preferable (economy, redundancy of the second asymmetry); remaining puzzle is the ordered distribution of matter in the early universe - a puzzle for cosmology; open mind warranted on smooth recollapse (Gold universe) and future low-entropy boundaries
proof_status: Conceptual argument; no calculations to reproduce
open_questions: Whether the 'absolutely forbidden' character of anti-thermodynamic processes breaks the parallel with Popper's pond (Callender SEP 3.2's contrast); what would count as evidence of a future low-entropy boundary
relevance: Primary source for the double-standard and Gold-universe positions the paper attributes to Price in sec:direction
limits: Large sections read, not every section (inflation-era cosmology section not sliced); the 1996 book's chs. 1-4, quoted by page in main.tex, were not accessed
